approach: Publication 1: Developed an 8-min mp-qMRI protocol based on Olsson et al.'s 7T work, adapted for 3T using mGRE (TR=30ms, FA=5/32) and EPI for B1 mapping. Validated in phantoms, 5 healthy volunteers (scanned on two Siemens scanners), and 4 BT patients. Assessed accuracy against reference methods and inter-scanner reproducibility using COV and Bland-Altman plots. Publication 2: Compared three MRS quantification methods in 5 healthy volunteers and 1 BT patient: (1) Reference method (literature values for relaxation/correction), (2) Reference method with qMRI (gold standard, using actual qMRI maps), and (3) Proposed method (synthesizing water reference from qMRI H2O map + SV STEAM calibration). Used LCModel for fitting and Friedman’s rm-ANOVA for statistical comparison.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Developed a fast (8 min), vendor-neutral mp-qMRI protocol suitable for multicenter studies. Demonstrated that qMRI-based water content mapping can replace redundant MRS water reference acquisitions without loss of quantification accuracy.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Inter-scanner reproducibility tested only within the same vendor (Siemens); inter-vendor compatibility remains unverified. The protocol uses interpolated resolution (1.2mm to 1mm) which may affect apparent resolution. The proposed MRS method assumes a constant correction factor for T2 estimation from T2* in the STEAM voxel, which may introduce error if the assumption does not hold universally. Large brain tumors may suffer from underestimation of water content due to bias field correction issues.

key_findings.conditions: Phantoms and healthy volunteers; compared to reference T1 mapping
key_findings.finding: The proposed mp-qMRI protocol showed good agreement with reference methods (<1% difference in T1). Inter-scanner reproducibility was high for T1, H2O, and T2* (COV <14%), but unreliable for χ due to near-zero values.

The 'Reference method' (using literature values) significantly underestimated metabolite concentrations compared to methods using individual-specific corrections ('Ref-method-with-qMRI' and 'Proposed method').

The 'Reference method' overestimated metabolite concentrations in healthy tissue and underestimated them in tumor regions (~15% lower than proposed method) due to inaccurate literature assumptions for pathological tissue.
No significant differences were observed between the gold standard qMRI-corrected method and the proposed synthesis method. Bias was <0.5%, reducing total scan time by ~8 minutes.

problem_or_question: Standard weighted MRI is insufficient for predicting tumor biology per WHO 2021 guidelines. Existing qMRI protocols are too long (~20+ min) for clinical routine. Additionally, accurate absolute quantification of MRS metabolites requires correcting for water relaxation effects, traditionally done via redundant, time-consuming acquisitions or inaccurate literature values.
research_scope: 3T MRI scanners (Siemens Prisma and Skyra); healthy volunteers (n=5) and brain tumor patients (n=4-5); phantoms. Focuses on developing a fast multi-parametric quantitative MRI (mp-qMRI) protocol and applying it to absolute quantification of cerebral metabolites via MR Spectroscopy (MRS).
work_summary: This dissertation presents two methodological developments for brain tumor imaging. First, it introduces an 8-minute, vendor-neutral mp-qMRI protocol using generalized sequences (mGRE and EPI) to simultaneously map T1, T2*, H2O, and susceptibility (χ). Second, it proposes a novel method for absolute quantification of MRSI metabolites by synthesizing the spectroscopic water reference from the qMRI-derived H2O map, calibrated by a single-voxel STEAM sequence, thereby eliminating the need for a time-consuming separate water reference scan.
